In standard macroeconomic theory with a proportional income tax rate t, disposable income is Y_d = (1 - t)Y, giving aggregate demand C + I = c(1 - t)Y + A. The multiplier is k = 1 / [1 - c(1 - t)].
Given marginal propensity to consume c = 0.8 and tax rate t = 0.25 (25%), the denominator is 1 - 0.8(1 - 0.25) = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4.
The correct multiplier is k = 1 / 0.4 = 2.5.
